title: Constructible algebraic numbers characterized by Galois groups

problemStatement.plain: An algebraic number α is constructible by compass and straightedge if and only if the Galois group of its minimal polynomial over ℚ is a 2-group (has order a power of 2).
whyMatters: Explains angle trisection impossibility: cos(20°) has Galois group S₃ of order 6
Connects classical Greek geometry to modern Galois theory

proven: 6 is not a power of 2 (coprimality: gcd(3,2)=1, so 3∤2^n, but 3|6)
Gal(8x³-6x-1/ℚ) is NOT a 2-group (order 6) — cos(20°) not constructible

insights: IsFiniteDimensional does not exist in Mathlib4 — use FiniteDimensional (the typeclass)
finrank not available as open name in current Mathlib — use Module.finrank instead
omega cannot prove 6 = 2^n → False (exponentials not linear) — use coprimality instead
IsPGroup.of_card takes implicit n: Nat.card G = p^n; use 'show Nat.card G = 2^k from ...' to specify k
not_pow_two_of_eq_six: if 6 = 2^n, then Nat.Coprime 3 (2^n) (from gcd(3,2)=1), and 3 | 2^n (from h), so 3 | gcd 3 (2^n) = 1, contradiction by norm_num
